newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - July 30.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - July 30.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Philippine stocks on Wednesday:

* Investors await the release of more company earnings for the first half of the year and results are likely to dictate the market's pace, traders said. Uncertainties in the financial markets continue to provide negative undertones, they added.
* "We believe that trading over the next few weeks will hinge largely on corporate results as investors re-evaluate full-year corporate prospects," said BPI Securities Corp analyst Spencer Yap.
* "Our position continues to be one of caution given the possible uncertainties looming from national elections next year; a short-term position seems the best course," added Yap.
* On Tuesday, the Philippine composite index closed slightly higher by 0.25 points at 2,592.46 points.
* The Dow Jones on Tuesday ended 53.42 points higher at 8,174.53c PLDT's ADR closed lower by $0 3/8 at $32 1/4.
* The Philippine peso ended at 28.50 to a dollar vs 28.479
* The Philippine interbank call loan average was at 22.03125 percent vs 25.03125 percent.
* President Fidel Ramos said early campaigning for presidential elections still 10 months away would derail the Philippines' economic momentum.
* Vitarich Corp said it made 33.018 million pesos for the first six months of the year from a loss of 496.73 million loss a year ago.
* Alcorn Petroleum & Minerals Corp said it posted a 4.65 million peso net income for the first half of the year from 2.99 million last year.

* Several major banks in the Philippines cut their prime lending rates on Tuesday, a day after the central bank brought down its closely-watched overnight borrowing rate by three percentage points to 22 percent. However, the rate adjustments were less than three percentage points, treasurers and corporate bankers said.

* Foreign banks operating in Manila said on Tuesday they could cope with new controls on their behaviour which are meant to ease pressure on the embattled peso. The Bankers Association of the Philippines recommended on Monday the exclusion of foreign banks from the spot foreign exchange market to reduce demand for the U.S. currency.

* Union Bank of the Philippines is expected to register a net income of around 300 million pesos in the second quarter of the year, a bank official said. The bank posted a 300.2 million peso net income in the first three months of the year.
* Ayala Land Inc said it had bought 112 hectares of land in the industrial Cavite province from the foreclosed Manila Banking Corp.
* First Philippine Holdings Corp said it had incorporated a new wholly-owned subsidiary which will construct and operate an oil pipeline north of Manila.
* Reynolds Philippines Corp said it was negotiating for the sale of its holdings in three joint venture firms with Malaysia's Leader Universal Holdings Bhd.
* La Tondena Distillers Inc, an affiliate of San Miguel Corp said its first six months net income rose to 280 million pesos from 220 million a year ago.
* The Bank of Philippine Islands said it made 1,208 million pesos for the second quarter of the year.
* Atlas Consolidated Mining and Development said a proposed take over by a new investor into the company would be presented at its shareholders meeting today.
* Security Bank Corp said it made 219.16 million pesos in net income for the second quarter of the year.

* Newspaper BusinessWorld said quoting a senior but anonymous National Economic and Development Authority (Neda) official that the Development Budget Coordinating Council will start to review the government's seven to eight percent gross national product (GNP) growth target in a meeting on Thursday.
